dovish.title: September Payrolls Cracked: +29k vs ~90k; Prior Months Revised 60k Lower
dovish.summary: The labor market cracked in September: payrolls +29k against a ~90k street, unemployment up to 4.2%, July-August revised a combined 60k lower, and wages up only 0.1% m/m — the October hike debate has flipped toward hold.
dovish.source: BLS Employment Situation, September 2026 (released Oct 2 08:30 ET; official series via the BLS public API — the bls.gov release page returned HTTP 403 this round; wire mirror bound)

data.unit: thousand jobs, m/m change, seasonally adjusted (September 2026)

dovish.reason: The September Employment Situation (released Oct 2, 08:30 ET) is the fissure: payrolls +29k against a ~90k street, with July revised down 31k to -10k and August down 29k to +133k — a combined -60k revision that raises the bar for calling this noise. Unemployment rose to 4.2% on rising participation (61.8%); average hourly earnings slowed to +0.1% m/m (3.0% y/y). Health care (+17k) and construction (+11k) carried what little job creation there was. For the Fed's reaction function this is the strongest dovish entry since the Sep 16 hike: it removes the labor-market argument for another hike at Oct 28. Weight 2.0 — the month's flagship release, a ~61k headline miss with negative net revisions; the card moved from the hawkish side per the refresh rule because the reading reversed. Market validation: ZN=F +0.25% across the release window; CAD futures +0.11%.

decision_brief.authoring_note: Written from scratch for the 2026-10-03 snapshot after the full fresh recollection (see evidence/recollection/), including the newly captured October 2 September Employment Situation; no sentence is carried over from the 2026-10-02 brief.
decision_brief.headline: September payrolls cracked (+29k vs ~90k; July-August revised 60k lower; unemployment 4.2%) — the October hike tail should deflate, though nothing verifiable is dislocated enough to trade yet.
decision_brief.summary: Friday resolved the week's swing factor to the weak side: the September Employment Situation showed payrolls of just +29k against ~90k expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%, average hourly earnings +0.1% m/m (3.0% y/y), and July-August revised a combined 60k lower — the clearest labor-market crack of this cycle, and the end of the 'labor still tight, another hike possible' story for October 28. Both central banks remain on hold (Fed 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28; BoC 2.25% into Oct 28), and the verifiable contracts sit just off policy: ZQV26 closed 96.120 on Friday, implying a 3.88% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR (+0.5 bp over the 3.875% range midpoint; its average is set mostly before the Oct 28 decision), while CRAU26's quote side (bid 97.6525 / ask 97.655; no executed print at the weekend capture) implies roughly 2.346% quarterly average CORRA (+9.6 bp over target) across the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions. Neither is a meeting probability and CME FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no direct single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot. The tape split: the front end agreed with the data (ZN=F +0.25% across the release window; SPY closed +0.74% at 769.64) while the long end kept bleeding (TLT -0.30% d, -2.32% w) — a front-end story, not a duration one. The rope now leans dovish (net -1.0) on the refreshed payrolls card plus JOLTS (-256k), against a hawkish side that is intact but small (core PCE 3.0% y/y; ISM prices-paid 77.9; Michigan expectations 4.6%). The read: the hike conversation is over for now; the open question is how soon the next two meetings move from hold toward easing — and there is still no verifiable way to size that from here.

The contract averages almost the whole month before the Oct 28 decision, so it measures October's starting regime, not the meeting's outcome. Separately, media coverage (AlphaPilot, Oct 1, citing CME FedWatch) reported market-implied odds of another hike on Oct 28 above 70% — that figure predates Friday's payrolls print, which removed its labor argument, and this environment cannot verify it (direct FedWatch requests return HTTP 403); stale context, not data. The genuine surprise risk now runs both ways: a market positioned for hike-tail was just handed a 61k headline miss with -60k of revisions.

Chasing the move: the front end already rallied on Friday's print (ZN +0.25% on the window); entering after the fact fights a hold-to-easing repricing not yet confirmed by a second data point (services Oct 5, claims Oct 8).
Duration trap: the long end ignored the weak labor data (TLT fell again Friday, -2.32% w) — a duration-long view based on soft data alone would have lost this week and can again.
BoC asymmetry: the hawkish column is empty by absence, not by evidence; a strong Ivey print or trade rebound (Oct 6) removes the dovish lean with no new BoC communication.
Stale-mark risk: marks are Friday's close; the next prints land Monday-Wednesday. Re-price before sizing.

fed.stance: Hold at 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28 — the September report cracked the hike tail; no verifiable meeting distribution
fed.rationale: The Sep 16 FOMC raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%; Friday's September Employment Situation is the first hard evidence since: +29k vs ~90k, unemployment 4.2%, and a combined -60k revision to July-August — the labor argument for another hike is gone, and wages (+0.1% m/m, 3.0% y/y) softened too. The counterweight is inflation (core PCE 3.0% y/y; ISM prices-paid 77.9; Michigan 1-year expectations 4.6%). FedWatch returned HTTP 403 again, so no single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot; ZQV26 closed 96.120 (3.88% October average, +0.5 bp over the range midpoint) — the pre-decision regime, not the meeting. Net: hold is the strong base case, and the next debate is when an easing bias appears.

The BoC side of the watcher does not get a US-labor-market read-through for free: domestic data has to show it.

decision_brief.trade_status_rationale: Deliberate abstention with a stated view. The view: the September report cracked the hike tail and the rope reads dovish (net -1.0) for the first time in this chain — the Fed holds Oct 28 and the next debate is when an easing bias appears. The reason it is not a trade from here: neither board has a verifiable single-meeting distribution (FedWatch HTTP 403 again) and every verifiable contract sits within a few bp of policy (October Fed average +0.5 bp over midpoint; CORRA +9.6 bp over target) — there is no dislocated price to express the view in, and Friday's front-end rally already anticipates confirmation that the next data (services Oct 5, claims Oct 8) has not yet delivered.
